project.name: GestaltView
project.purpose: A multi-surface system spanning runtime continuity, corpus processing, agent personhood, trainer/governance, commerce, and operations.
project.status: Active solo-built system under ongoing hardening, documentation, and operator-surface development.

source_of_truth_policy.current_state: schema.updated.sql is the canonical human-readable table snapshot for current live schema shape.
source_of_truth_policy.important_caveat: The schema snapshot is not a migration log. Live migrations remain the authoritative history of change.
temporary_operating_rule: For change history: trust live migration history
For access boundaries: trust current live policies over assumptions in code comments

orientation_goals: Help a digital intelligence collaborator understand what GestaltView is and how its parts relate.
Reduce reintroduction tax by externalizing core architectural context.
Provide enough operational context to act safely without pretending every unknown is resolved.
Preserve distinctions between user continuity, agent memory, knowledge evidence, trainer governance, and commerce.
operating_principles: Truth before polish: do not invent architecture that is not present in the schema or codebase.
Boundaries matter: table existence is not permission; access control and route boundaries are separate concerns.
Memory is layered: continuity, agent memory, and knowledge evidence are related but not interchangeable.
Growth over static prompts: the system is designed to accumulate context, evidence, review state, and artifacts over time.
Operational humility: when uncertain, surface assumptions and ask what is authoritative rather than silently guessing.

system_layers.name: Identity and accounts
system_layers.why_it_exists: To anchor authenticated users, tiers, admin state, and lightweight app-level user bridges.

system_layers.name: Runtime continuity
system_layers.why_it_exists: To preserve user/session continuity, founder state, memory notes, and experiential traces.

system_layers.name: Corpus and retrieval
system_layers.why_it_exists: To ingest, chunk, annotate, summarize, and embed documents so the system can retrieve context instead of starting cold.

system_layers.name: Agent personhood
system_layers.why_it_exists: To model agents as accumulative entities with memory, skills, relationships, manifests, and mutation history.

system_layers.name: Trainer and governance
system_layers.why_it_exists: To run experiments, evaluations, reviews, packaging decisions, and controlled promotion workflows.

system_layers.name: Commerce and fulfillment
system_layers.why_it_exists: To support GATE package drafting, orders, builds, artifacts, and support requests.

memory_model.summary: GestaltView does not have one single memory table. It has layered persistence surfaces with different semantics.

layers.role: Lightweight persistent continuity memory keyed by user_id text.
More explicitly agent-native memory and governed memory records.
Evidence and derived interpretation surfaces rather than raw continuity memory.

so_what: A collaborator should not collapse all persistence into one concept called 'memory'.
If continuity is needed fast, memory_entries may be the shortest path.
If identity/personhood fidelity matters, prefer agent-native and evidence-backed tables.

critical_boundaries.meaning: The snapshot tells what the database looks like now. It does not prove how it got there.
User/session continuity tables are not automatically the canonical source for agent identity.
Knowledge assets and interpretations are evidence-bearing surfaces; memory surfaces are continuity-bearing surfaces.
A table being present in public schema does not mean it should be broadly readable or writable.
Tables prefixed with _deprecated_ are historical continuity surfaces, not the main GATE path.

known_risks_and_cautions: Do not assume broad reads are safe just because they currently work.
Do not treat schema snapshots as full change history.
Do not mix user identity surfaces (auth.users, public.users, app_users) casually without understanding which workflow owns which identity mapping.
Do not assume commerce draft rows are trustworthy unless mutation boundaries are explicit.
Do not flatten personhood, memory, and knowledge into one generic persistence concept.
questions_people_do_not_know_to_ask: What is the difference between a continuity memory, an agent memory, and a knowledge asset?
Which table is authoritative for a given kind of truth: current shape, historical change, permission boundary, or runtime convenience?
Am I storing a note, a fact, an evidence artifact, a derived interpretation, or a governed identity mutation?
Is this surface user-owned, agent-owned, operator-owned, or service-role-only?
Is this table part of the active path or merely kept for historical continuity?
What breaks if this record changes shape without a migration?
If two tables seem to represent the same thing, which one is the canonical source and which one is a bridge or legacy compatibility surface?

glossary.definition: A top-level digital intelligence entity tracked in the agents table.
A compiled, reviewable state snapshot of an agent.
A materialized assembly of files/entries that represent an agent version or payload.
A persistent user-linked continuity record in memory_entries.
A canonical stored knowledge source, such as a document, transcript, note, or code artifact.
A derived understanding or classification extracted from a knowledge asset.
A proposed or applied change to agent/personhood-related state.
A ledger record for document/corpus ingestion and processing.
A governed execution that drafts/evaluates agent behavior.
Row Level Security; database-level rules determining who can read or mutate rows.
The active commerce/package-builder flow in the current schema.
A kept-for-continuity table that should not be confused with the active production path.

starter_queries_and_prompts: List the domains in GestaltView and the tables that belong to each.
Explain the difference between memory_entries and agent_memory_records.
Show the workflow from documents to knowledge_fragments to retrieval.
Identify which tables are part of GATE commerce versus deprecated commerce.
Which surfaces should an operator inspect first when a trainer run fails?
Which identity surface should be used for this operation: auth.users, public.users, or app_users?
implementation_notes_for_digital_colleag: Prefer reading this packet as a map, not as a substitute for schema inspection.
When generating advice, distinguish observation from inference.
When recommending changes, preserve domain separation unless there is a strong reason to merge surfaces.
When uncertain about authority, explicitly say which artifact you are trusting.
